views.label: Protocol ↔ Envelope
Strict ↔ Loose

method: Eight choices every card makes: naming, identity, discovery, type (media type, and whether it is registered), encoding, extension, trust, versioning.
Quoted from the specs. Each value is taken from the card's spec at a commit: 30 spec versions, 269 quotes, each checked against the line it cites. Every tick links to the spec at that commit.
Centre. On each date, the value most cards share for each choice.
Distance. How many of a card's eight choices no other card makes. Leaving a choice open ("none", "not specified") does not count as a choice.
A card can move without changing. Distance depends on the other cards: when one spec changes, what counts as shared changes for every card. On 2026-08-26 AI Catalog moved because ARD changed.

Above or below. Protocol ↔ Envelope: cards defined by one protocol (A2A, MCP Server Card) sit above; protocol-neutral envelopes (AI Catalog, ARD, .fafa) sit below. Strict ↔ Loose: each card's required-field count against the median of the cards present.
Distance means different, not wrong. .fafa sits furthest out partly because it is the only card with an IANA-registered media type, and the only one written in YAML.
The choice list is a judgement. A different list would draw a different map. The list and every quote sit behind the map, so anyone can check it or redraw it.

cells.label: name
cells.evidence: string name = 1 [(google.api.field_behavior) = REQUIRED];
cells.note: Unchanged from v1.0.0.

cells.label: url
cells.evidence: The URL where this interface is available. Must be a valid absolute HTTPS URL in production.
cells.note: Unchanged: endpoint in REQUIRED `supportedInterfaces[].url` (L339). Changed nearby: optional AgentInterface.tenant is now described as "An opaque string used for routing requests to a specific agent or tenant when multiple agents are served behind a single A2A endpoint" (L344-L345); the protocol "does not define its format or semantics" (L349).

cells.label: /.well-known/agent-card.json
cells.evidence: Accessing `https://{server_domain}/.well-known/agent-card.json`
cells.note: §14.3 template unchanged (L3328, L3337). IANA's well-known URI registry lists `agent-card.json` as permanent (checked 2026-09-15).

cells.label: none · none
cells.evidence: The resource at this URI MUST return an AgentCard object as defined in Section 4.4.1 of the A2A specification.
cells.note: Still no media type for the card at the well-known URI. Changed here: the REST binding now says "application/a2a+json **SHOULD** be used for requests and responses" (L2750), which covers `GET /extendedAgentCard`; the JSON-RPC binding keeps `application/json` (L2236). `application/a2a+json` is still not in IANA's application registry (checked 2026-09-15).

cells.label: json
cells.evidence: A JSON metadata document published by an A2A Server, describing its identity, capabilities, skills, service endpoint, and authentication requirements.
cells.note: Unchanged: proto is normative; JSON uses camelCase (§5.5, L1204).

cells.label: capabilities.extensions
cells.evidence: A list of protocol extensions supported by the agent.
cells.note: `repeated AgentExtension extensions = 3;` (L417). Unchanged.

cells.label: jws-signature
cells.evidence: Agent Cards **MAY** be digitally signed using JSON Web Signature (JWS)
cells.note: Unchanged: JCS (RFC 8785) canonicalization before signing (L2008); `signatures` optional (proto L395).

cells.label: supportedInterfaces[].protocolVersion
cells.evidence: The version of the A2A protocol this interface exposes.
cells.note: REQUIRED (L354). Unchanged. Appendix A.2.1 still mentions an AgentCard `protocolVersions` field (L3509, L3517).

cells.label: title (optional)
cells.evidence: Optional human-readable title or display name for the MCP server.
cells.note: `title?: string` (L81). Clients read `title` from the card, not the catalog entry (docs/discovery.md L54-L55).

cells.label: reverse-dns
cells.evidence: Server name in reverse-DNS format. Must contain exactly one forward slash
cells.note: Pattern `^[a-zA-Z0-9.-]+/[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$` (L50). The valid example examples/ServerCard/valid/minimal.json uses `example-org/minimal`, with no dot. Catalog-level identifier: `urn:air:{publisher}:{namespace}:{name}` (docs/discovery.md L48).

cells.label: via:/.well-known/ai-catalog.json
cells.evidence: Fetch `https://{domain}/.well-known/ai-catalog.json`
cells.note: Card location: 'MCP Servers MAY host their Server Card at `GET <streamable-http-url>/server-card`, which we reserve for this purpose, though any unreserved URI (on any domain) is valid' (L174-L175). SEP 5c8483d L90: 'Cards can be hosted at any unreserved URI, with `<streamable-http-url>/server-card` reserved as the recommended location.'

cells.label: application/mcp-server-card+json · de-facto
cells.evidence: Server Cards use the media type `application/mcp-server-card+json`.
cells.note: Not in the IANA application media-type registry (checked 2026-09-15); the only 'mcp' matches are unrelated vnd.3gpp.mcptt-* types. Clients SHOULD send `Accept: application/mcp-server-card+json` (L182).

cells.label: json
cells.evidence: An **MCP Server Card** is a JSON document that describes a single MCP server

cells.label: _meta
cells.evidence: extension metadata, which remains the card's extension point.
cells.note: The line begins 'Vendors who genuinely need to attach install hints to a Server Card can use namespaced [`_meta`]'. schema.ts L115 and L121 define `_meta?: MetaObject`. SEP 5c8483d L89: '`_meta` is not used to advertise MCP capabilities or negotiated extension support.'

cells.label: none
cells.evidence: Clients MUST NOT treat Server Card contents as authoritative for security or
cells.note: Advisory only. The 'Server Card Accuracy' security note (L229-L238) calls an inaccurate card 'a mild confusion or downgrade vector'. Hosted cards MUST use HTTPS, TLS 1.2 or later, in production (L273). No signature or trust manifest.

cells.label: $schema, version, remotes[].supportedProtocolVersions
cells.evidence: Schema URLs are versioned by the `vN` segment rather than by date; a
cells.note: $schema must equal `https://static.modelcontextprotocol.io/schemas/v1/server-card.schema.json` (L35, L40). version = server version, 'Equivalent of `Implementation.version`' (L55-L57). remotes[].supportedProtocolVersions = 'MCP protocol versions actively supported by this remote endpoint' (L199-L202). README.md L63: 'The `v1` shape is still pre-release and card-only'.

cells.label: displayName (optional)
cells.evidence: ? displayName: text,
cells.note: Prose: listed under OPTIONAL (L259, L261). Resolution order (L342): entry displayName, then the artifact's own name, then the identifier's trailing segment.

cells.label: urn:air
cells.evidence: the standard `urn:air` naming structure is **HIGHLY RECOMMENDED** and **MUST** be used for open or federated systems.
cells.note: Open-text field ('any valid URI or URN is accepted', same line). Format `urn:air:{publisher}:{namespace}:{name}` (L209).

cells.label: /.well-known/ai-catalog.json
cells.evidence: /.well-known/ai-catalog.json
cells.note: OPTIONAL; a catalog MAY be served from any URL. Link relation `ai-catalog` (L1256). Registration sections: link relation (L1629), well-known URI (L1645). Neither is in the IANA registries (checked 2026-09-15); IANA lists only RFC 9727 `api-catalog`.

cells.label: application/ai-catalog+json · de-facto
cells.evidence: application/ai-catalog+json
cells.note: Registration section L1582. `curl https://www.iana.org/assignments/media-types/application.csv | grep -i catalog` on 2026-09-15 returns no ai-catalog entry.

cells.label: json
cells.evidence: An AI Catalog document is a JSON object that MUST contain the following

cells.label: extensions-map
cells.evidence: represent the extension type (namespace), and the corresponding value contains the extension data.
cells.note: Keys 'MUST be a valid URL or a reverse-DNS string' (L1121-1122). Entry `extensions` L326; catalog top level L151; Trust Manifest L612.

cells.label: trust-manifest+jws
cells.evidence: contain at least one *substantive* trust member:
cells.note: `trustManifest` is OPTIONAL (L553-555). Trust Manifest `signature` is a detached JWS (L604-605); optional top-level catalog `signature` JWS (L156-157). The CDDL still lacks the top-level `signature` (L1670-1675) and TrustManifest `subject`/`issuedAt`/`expiresAt` (L1709-1719).

cells.label: specVersion
cells.evidence: `specVersion`
cells.note: 'Major.Minor' format (L104); Version Handling section L1174.

cells.label: displayName
cells.evidence: | displayName | MUST | Human-readable name. |
cells.note: Row of the table introduced by 'An ARD entry MUST carry:' (L86).

cells.label: urn:air
cells.evidence: Domain-anchored URN form (`urn:air:<publisher>:<namespace>:<agent-name>`); see Appendix C.
cells.note: The JSON-LD @id MAY mirror the identifier (L90). ard-entry.schema.json pattern ^urn:air:... (L26).

cells.label: /.well-known/ard.json
cells.evidence: Hosting a manifest of entries at `https://{domain}/.well-known/ard.json`.
cells.note: Link relation: rel="ard" (L199). A consumer MUST fetch /.well-known/ard.json and MUST honour rel="ard"; it MAY also consult the predecessor /.well-known/ai-catalog.json and rel="ai-catalog" (L202). A publisher on the predecessor path SHOULD move to ard.json (L204). In-page JSON-LD markup (L197), Agentmap and DNS (L200) are also listed.

cells.label: none · none
cells.evidence: The manifest is a JSON document with an `entries` array of ARD entries (§4)
cells.note: No media type is defined for the manifest document. Entry `type` is the artifact's IANA media type (L92); registries are found through entries whose type is application/ai-registry+json (L215). The application/ai-catalog+json nested-catalog examples are gone.

cells.label: json-ld
cells.evidence: An entry is a JSON-LD node describing an agentic resource.
cells.note: Per entry. A consumer MUST expand an entry with the ARD base context (L80; spec/schemas/ard.context.jsonld). Carrying @context in the entry is OPTIONAL (L82). The /.well-known/ard.json manifest itself is 'a JSON document' (L196).

cells.label: json-ld-context
cells.evidence: Terms from any additional namespace declared in the entry's `@context` MAY also appear
cells.note: Such terms become filter dimensions with no spec change (L108). `metadata` remains an optional descriptive term (L106). The schema sets additionalProperties: true by design (L530); ard.cddl ard-entry ends with a `* tstr => any` wildcard (L25).

cells.label: trust-manifest
cells.evidence: ARD does not define a signing or verification procedure of its own.
cells.note: trustManifest is optional; ARD requires only trustManifest.identity (L173), whose trust domain MUST align with the URN publisher (L177). Signing, canonicalization and key resolution come from the framework named in trustManifest.trustSchema (L181). ard-entry.schema.json L170 no longer names JWS. The schema's entry property key is `TrustManifest` (L81); the spec, ard.cddl (L45) and the base context use `trustManifest`.

cells.label: not specified
cells.evidence: ARD requires only an `entries` array of ARD entries
cells.note: ArdManifest requires only entries (L106); other top-level members are transport-defined and ignored by ARD. ard.cddl ard-manifest is entries plus a wildcard (L13-L15). specVersion is no longer defined. The base context URL ends /context/v1 (spec L78) and entry `version` is the artifact version; neither is a spec-version field.

cells.label: agent.name
cells.evidence: **Required:** `name` (Unicode string, unique within the issuing vendor namespace)
cells.note: The spec text still has no display-name field. The companion schema schemas/fafa.schema.json documents an optional `agent.displayName` from 9e79b6914b6cb0ef6df299e52de17ccc47657a5e (2026-07-05), and FAFA's published card uses it (agent.fafa L9). See notes.

cells.label: agent-id
cells.evidence: `id` (globally unique identifier — DID, URI, or vendor-scoped UUID)
cells.note: Practice: FAFA's card uses `id: did:web:faf.one:agent`.

cells.label: none
cells.evidence: It does not define discovery, transport, authorization, or orchestration.
cells.note: Spec unchanged. Practice only (not in spec): faf.one serves FAFA's card at /.well-known/fafa with Content-Type application/vnd.fafa+yaml (checked 2026-09-15). The one well-known URI request filed is for /.well-known/faf (protocol-registries/well-known-uris#97, open, labels 'new registration' and 'waiting for stable reference'). No request covers /.well-known/fafa.

cells.label: application/vnd.fafa+yaml · iana-registered
cells.evidence: (registered 2026-06-26, last updated 2026-06-26)
cells.note: Spec at this SHA: L5 '**MIME Type:** `application/vnd.fafa+yaml`', L7 '**IANA Registration:** Registered 2026-06-26 (vendor tree)' (https://github.com/Wolfe-Jam/faf/blob/190c3380847c022da3e13a28af57c4dc68b3e02c/AGENT-FORMAT.md#L7). The IANA record's 'Published specification' is https://github.com/Wolfe-Jam/faf/blob/main/AGENT-FORMAT.md.

cells.label: yaml
cells.evidence: A `.fafa` file is a single YAML document:

cells.label: metadata-object
cells.evidence: **Optional top-level fields:** `attachment`, `provenance`, `signature`, `metadata` (free-form vendor extensions).
cells.note: §13 (L219): forward-compat rule for unknown top-level fields and unknown agent/capabilities/endpoints subfields. It does not name `provenance` subfields.

cells.label: other:optional signature object (method, value); signing scheme unspecified
cells.evidence: Where present, `signature` carries provenance/integrity material; verification is the consumer's responsibility.
cells.note: Unchanged. FAFA's published card carries no `signature` block.

cells.label: version
cells.evidence: The top-level `version` field declares which version of this specification the document conforms to.
cells.note: Spec §16 (L252) lists 'Optional parameters: version', but the IANA record says 'Optional parameters: N/A' and 'versioning is handled in-band via the top-level "version" field'.

server_json.name: MCP Registry server.json

adoption.claim: 32,237 latest-version server entries in the official registry, counted page by page from the live API on 2026-09-15T16:34Z
The registry repo has 7,251 stars and 36 releases (latest v1.8.1, 2026-08-06), checked 2026-09-15
AI Catalog names 'an MCP Registry `server.json`' as an artifact whose own version a consumer may read (line added 2026-07-23, commit 2b5afb9f263f7a7252bcac0a1ad3b61a6fdea599)

server_json.relation: CONFIRMED: SEP-2127 Rev 1 borrowed the server.json shape. The first git draft (3bb8831, 2026-01-21) has no server.json reference and no remotes/packages fields (https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/blob/3bb8831844ed142c1f81858aff610d12a0755c79/seps/2127-mcp-server-cards.md). Rev 1 (PR #2152 merged 2026-01-30, commit e105d30) says 'Most fields follow the current MCP Registry `server.json` standard' (https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/blob/e105d30b6264d957050389c0b0edf3ceae2a8224/seps/2127-mcp-server-cards.md#L287), adds remotes/packages (https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/blob/e105d30b6264d957050389c0b0edf3ceae2a8224/seps/2127-mcp-server-cards.md#L79), and has a section 'Why Mirror `server.json`'s shape?' (https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/blob/e105d30b6264d957050389c0b0edf3ceae2a8224/seps/2127-mcp-server-cards.md#L410). Two days later (2195161, 2026-02-01): 'We rename the MCP Registry's `server.json` to `Extended MCP Server Card`' (https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/blob/2195161c41a2a03a0bc559bd2ef7c7430e77b963/seps/2127-mcp-server-cards.md#L301). 2026-03-23 (cfe7de2, 'Align Server Card with server.json'): 'Local, stdio-based servers should plan to distribute via `server.json` and the MCP Registry.' (https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/blob/cfe7de2787ddc7cc28eb7504554db31d6162fcc0/seps/2127-mcp-server-cards.md#L306). Latest (5c8483d, 2026-08-24) separates them: 'The Registry owns that schema; the Server Card extension does not define a `Server` superset or package-installation types.' (https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/blob/5c8483d511d60ef1f8ded5160c5290fd8213d19e/seps/2127-mcp-server-cards.md#L72). The extension repo agrees: server.json 'is owned by the registry, not by this extension' (https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-server-card/blob/526201bbc80231daa40ffcdecfc9da4e54e5dc93/README.md#L25). Precursor: the Server Card idea first appeared as issue SEP-1649 (2025-10-14, closed 2026-01-26, proposing .well-known/mcp.json), which has no git history (https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/issues/1649). AI Catalog cites server.json as a referenced artifact (see adoption). server.json's own first schema calls itself 'Schema for a static representation of an MCP server.' (https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/blob/2061151d45991456de767f903855e2a75664b659/docs/server-json/schema.json#L4).

draw.name: ANP Agent Description (AD) document (ANP-07)

draw.name: agents.json (Wildcard)

draw.name: AGNTCY OASF record (Open Agentic Schema Framework)
draw.owner: AGNTCY project (Cisco-originated; Linux Foundation project since 2025-07-29) — repo agntcy/oasf

consider.name: Open Resource Discovery (ORD) document: Agent resource
consider.owner: SAP; README says governed by Linux Foundation / NeoNephos
consider.reason: Registered well-known, foundation governance and versioned git tags. But ORD is an enterprise resource catalog where Agent is one entity type, marked BETA in the docs. Its role is closer to AI Catalog than to a per-agent card.

consider.name: RFC 9727 api-catalog
consider.reason: Not agent-specific, but it is the documented precursor of AI Catalog's catalog role. Consider it as a predecessor station on the AI Catalog line rather than its own card.

consider.name: Eclipse LMOS Agent Description Format
consider.reason: Foundation-backed agent description with git history, but the spec pages have had no commits since 2025-04-10. Draw it only if the map shows the WoT branch.

consider.name: AGNTCY Agent Connect Protocol - Agent ACP Descriptor (Cisco-led 'ACP', not IBM's)
consider.status: deprecated in favor of A2A; repo archived
consider.reason: Passes both tests: 'Describe all the ACP specs of an agent, including schemas and protocol features.' (openapi.json L1903). But it is mostly an invocation-schema descriptor inside an API. It lived three months (Feb to May 2025), and its discovery role passed to the OASF record.

consider.name: NANDA AgentFacts
consider.reason: Passes both tests literally, but its git history is one upload commit (2025-06-17) with no later change, so it draws as a single station. Which schema is authoritative is also contested: agentfacts.org names a different repo as official.

consider.name: AID: Agent Identity & Discovery (v1 named Agent Interface Discovery)
consider.owner: agentcommunity (Agent Community); IETF individual draft draft-nemethi-dawn-aid-00
consider.reason: Git history since 2025-07-05 and an IETF draft under the DAWN name. It is a DNS locator record rather than a full card, so it fits better as a connector than a line.

consider.name: ACP Registry agent entry (Agent Client Protocol, agent.schema.json)
consider.owner: agentclientprotocol (Agent Client Protocol project; AAIF proposal #1)
consider.reason: Strong adoption (42 agents, JetBrains index) and a pending AAIF proposal. It is a registry-entry and install format, so decide it together with MCP Registry server.json.

not drawn.name: W3C WoT Thing Description
not drawn.reason: Scoped to IoT Things, not agents. It enters the map only as LMOS's parent.

not drawn.name: xRegistry
not drawn.reason: A generic registry substrate, not an agent or server description.

not drawn.name: Microsoft 365 Copilot declarative agent manifest
not drawn.reason: The schema has clean public git history (8 dated versions), but it is packaging and configuration for one product: '...a declarative agent for third party developers to be deployed to Microsoft 365 Copilot' (v1.0 L3). It carries the agent's instructions and is never published for discovery, and Microsoft's own discovery path uses A2A Agent Cards.

not drawn.name: LangChain Agent Protocol (Agent object)
not drawn.reason: It is a protocol API. The Agent object (openapi.json L1497) exists only as a response from a running server, with no document published for discovery.

not drawn.name: Letta Agent File (.af)
not drawn.reason: It serializes agent state for transfer and checkpointing, not for discovery.

not drawn.name: Google ADK AgentConfig (YAML agent config)
not drawn.reason: It is config to create an agent, not a discovery or description document.

not drawn.name: Oracle Open Agent Specification (Agent Spec)
not drawn.reason: It is a build and configuration language for running agents, not a discovery document.

not drawn.name: Microsoft AgentSchema
not drawn.reason: It builds agents rather than describing them for discovery: 'AgentSchema is a client facing spec designed to make creating agents easier in a code first YAML file format.' (README L3).

not drawn.name: Agent Skills (SKILL.md)
not drawn.reason: An instruction file describing a skill, not an agent or server; out under test (b).

not drawn.name: OpenBindings Interface (OBI)
not drawn.reason: Passes both tests and holds an IANA well-known, but no adoption beyond its own project is visible.

not drawn.name: AGTP Agent Identity Document
not drawn.owner: Chris Hood / nomoticai (Nomotic AI); I-D draft-hood-independent-agtp
not drawn.reason: Passes both tests, but it is a single-author individual draft whose repo has 10 stars. Note the IANA registration; do not draw a line.

not drawn.name: Agent Name Service (ANS) registration + DNS records
not drawn.owner: GoDaddy (agentnameservice org; LICENSE 'Copyright 2025 GoDaddy Operating Company, LLC.') with IETF individual drafts by Narajala, Courtney, Huang, Habler, Sheriff
not drawn.reason: It is an identity, naming and trust layer: registration 'binds to operational metadata (display name, description, endpoints)' (ans-1 L11) and hands the description itself to the A2A card or MCP metadata through metaDataUrl. Worth a map annotation as the connector between A2A and ARD.

not drawn.name: AgentMug .agent file (application/vnd.agentmug.agent+json)
not drawn.reason: It is an executable agent definition ('A .agent file is a portable, declarative definition of an AI agent.', spec L14), not a discovery document.

not drawn.name: OpenAI ai-plugin.json (ChatGPT plugin manifest)
not drawn.reason: Fails (a): the manifest was defined on OpenAI docs pages, not in git, and OpenAI's repos hold only example manifests. No field can be quoted from a spec at a commit.

not drawn.name: AWS Agent Registry record (Amazon Bedrock AgentCore)
not drawn.reason: Docs only, with no git-versioned spec. Agent records reuse the A2A card, so there is no separate AWS card to draw.

not drawn.name: Claude Code plugin manifest (plugin.json) and marketplace.json
not drawn.reason: No normative spec with public git history was found (a public docs page only), and it describes a plugin bundle, not an agent or server.

borderline_mentions.name: AgentCard (draft-aevum-agentcard-00)
borderline_mentions.why: Individual I-D (2026-04-22, expires 2026-10-24) defining a framework-neutral 'AgentCard' JSON; no git repo found, so it fails (a) as far as checked; adoption unknown.

borderline_mentions.name: Agent Capability Advertisement Protocol / Agent Capability Documents (draft-zahed-acap-00)
borderline_mentions.why: I-D only (2026-06-25); defines ACDs served at a well-known URI; no git or adoption found.

borderline_mentions.name: ACPM capability profile and 'Autonomous Agent Interchange Format' (draft-schemacommons-acpm-00, draft-schemacommons-aaif-00)
borderline_mentions.why: I-Ds only (2026-06-25). The second uses the acronym AAIF, which collides with the Agentic AI Foundation; git not checked.

borderline_mentions.name: AI Agent Discovery and Invocation Protocol (draft-cui-ai-agent-discovery-invocation-02)
borderline_mentions.why: I-D defining a common agent metadata format; CATALIST-related; no git repo checked.

borderline_mentions.name: Metadata and Query Profile for Efficient Agent Discovery (draft-xu-efficient-agent-discovery-profile-00)
borderline_mentions.why: I-D-only JSON metadata profile (2026-05-18).

borderline_mentions.name: Minimum Discoverable Information model (draft-cui-dawn-mdi-model-00)
borderline_mentions.why: An information model, not a format; could become the DAWN baseline if the proposed WG adopts it. Watch.

borderline_mentions.name: ADP v1.1 well-known JSON metadata (draft-pro-adp-agent-discovery-02) and Walko Systems ADP /.well-known/agent-discovery.json
borderline_mentions.why: I-D only. The DAWN survey calls Walko's ADP single-author with one implementation; whether the two ADPs are the same was not verified.

borderline_mentions.name: AI Discovery Endpoint /.well-known/ai (draft-aiendpoint-ai-discovery-01)
borderline_mentions.why: I-D only; service self-description at /.well-known/ai, a name the IANA expert reserves for standards-based work.

borderline_mentions.name: IntentWeb AgentManifest (draft-jernalczyk-intentweb-agent-manifest-00)
borderline_mentions.why: Describes a website for visiting agents (site, not agent); I-D only.

borderline_mentions.name: DNS-AID (draft-mozleywilliams-dnsop-dnsaid-02; dns-aid/dns-aid-core)
borderline_mentions.why: DNS SVCB records under _agents (a locator, not a document); cited by ARD. Its README says it reads a native metadata doc at /.well-known/agent.json with aid_version; that format was not verified in the draft. The README also says A2A uses /.well-known/agent.json, but A2A's IANA-registered suffix is agent-card.json.

borderline_mentions.name: Agent Name Service (draft-narajala-courtney-ansv2-01; agentnameservice/ans)
borderline_mentions.why: Naming and registration protocol that relies on protocol-native cards; covered in vendor-and-merged.json.

borderline_mentions.name: BEST Behavioral State Protocol (/.well-known/best)
borderline_mentions.why: Service capability manifest for agents with git history and an I-D (draft-dinuzzo-best-protocol-01), but 4 stars and a single author; well-known request pre-check open (#104).

borderline_mentions.name: bluejetty
borderline_mentions.why: Commercial discovery descriptor pointing to 'app packets'; spec on a vendor docs site (git unverified); registration pending.

borderline_mentions.name: agents.txt / agents.json (kaylacar/agents-txt; draft-car-agents-txt-wellknown-00)
borderline_mentions.why: A different spec from the Wildcard agents.json covered elsewhere. It declares what visiting agents may do on a site, not an agent description. Registration refused; the expert called the repo private.

borderline_mentions.name: ai-disclosure.json (aidisclose.io)
borderline_mentions.why: Declares the AI systems a website operates, for transparency rules. Refused under the ai/agent naming policy; spec on a docs site, git unverified.

borderline_mentions.name: /.well-known/ai (rootz-global/ai-discovery)
borderline_mentions.why: Organisation profile for AI agents; registration refused; single company.

borderline_mentions.name: KCP Knowledge Context Protocol (Cantara)
borderline_mentions.why: Knowledge manifest (knowledge.yaml), close to context and instruction files; registration of 'kcp' refused.

borderline_mentions.name: flyweb.json
borderline_mentions.why: Site content manifest for agents (describes a site's content, not an agent); registration pending.

borderline_mentions.name: Docker MCP Registry server.yaml
borderline_mentions.why: 328 server.yaml entries describe MCP servers for Docker's catalog. It is a vendor submission format defined in CONTRIBUTING.md, a sibling of MCP Registry server.json.

borderline_mentions.name: agentregistry agent.yaml (agentregistry-dev/agentregistry)
borderline_mentions.why: 489-star product whose agent records bundle identity and MCP/skill dependencies; no standalone spec found.

borderline_mentions.name: Solid agent card (jeswr/solid-agent-card)
borderline_mentions.why: Combines an A2A Agent Card with an ANP RDF description for Solid; 0 stars.

borderline_mentions.name: agentrust-io/agent-manifest
borderline_mentions.why: Agent Manifest SDK from the TRACE proposers (AAIF proposal #42); spec status not verified.

borderline_mentions.name: agentpk (nomoticai/agentpk)
borderline_mentions.why: Agent packaging and signing 'standard' from the same org as AGTP; low adoption.

borderline_mentions.name: prime-vector/open-agent-spec
borderline_mentions.why: YAML agent definition, 19 stars; name overlaps Oracle's Open Agent Spec.

borderline_mentions.name: OpenBotAuth agent identity draft (draft-openbotauth-agent-identity-00)
borderline_mentions.why: Found by code search for 'Signature Agent Card' in docs/specs; not read.

borderline_mentions.name: W3C Agent Declaration and Assurance CG 'Open KYA Manifest Schema'
borderline_mentions.why: Planned only; the group page (started 2026-06-03) lists no draft.

borderline_mentions.name: AgentMug .agent (application/vnd.agentmug.agent+json)
borderline_mentions.why: Registered 2026-08-14. Covered in vendor-and-merged.json; listed here only because it came up in the IANA sweep.
